questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at Fantoft Sammen because it was an easy choice but as an exchange student you get a shared room with other exchange students. It was too much for me so i really tried to find other housing situations but it was hard as someone only living there for 5 months. In the end my new norwegian friend helped me through their contacts

Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took philosophy courses even though my major is ethnology. It was a bit stressful but not because of the reading or the level of academics. I thinks it was because it was a new way for me to write papers and learn. In the end i found the academic level was easier than what im used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is kinda the same. I don't think it the institutions that makes a teaching style. It's more the individual professors. I was lucky and found all my professors in Bergen to be really nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Wittgenstein Studies, Continental Philosophy and Moral Philosophy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved them all but the Wittgenstein was hard to understand completely. Would recommend them all but especially the moral philosophy one.

questions.answer: People in Bergen have a very professional clothing style but it was not challenging just surprised and not used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It a lovely experience but you will feel lonely at times and miss home and that's okay. But you will also learn stuff about yourself being alone and with new friends that will feel temporally but if you find the right friends maybe the friendships will last after the exchange is over. And also just try things even if it can be scary, you'll be happy you did it afterwards. but remind yourself it's okay to not have the typical erasmus experience.

questions.answer: Proving to myself that i could do it, find new friends that i really like and also succeed in taking phil. courses
